# Evidence

This page is the claims register: for every factual claim the wiki and the research documents make, it gives the source or reproducible check, the verbatim text or check ID, how it was checked, and the result.

Last reviewed: 1 Nov 2026

**How this page is made.** The page is generated by `research/evidence/render_evidence.py` from the register `research/evidence/claims.json` in the repository, so edit the register, not this page. `research/evidence/check_quotes.py` fetches every source that has a quote and confirms that the quote still appears in it. The Verified column gives the date of the last successful check. The register holds 86 claims: 56 verified, 18 quote corrected, 8 fetch failed, 4 unverified.

## How to read the register

- **Method.** *Fetched page*: the source page (or API response) was downloaded and the quote compared with its text after removing markup and collapsing whitespace. *Script check*: reproduced by [`research/verification/verify_claims.py`](https://github.com/Karthik-beta/fiscalclock/blob/main/research/verification/README.md), standard-library Python, rerun by CI; the ID is the check name. *Filing*: an SEC filing. *Secondary*: a source that is not the authority for the fact (Wikipedia, a forum post, an archived copy, or a summarised fetch).
- **Status.** *Verified*: the quote or value matches. *Quote corrected*: the source exists but the research documents' wording was not verbatim or overstated it; the corrected wording is given. *Fetch failed*: the script could not fetch the source (it never requests sec.gov); the row says how it was checked instead. *Unverified*: no authoritative source found; treat as an open question.
- The two research documents (the design proposal and the gap analysis) are not published; where a row says "proposal" or "gap analysis", it names the document that made the claim.

## SEC filings

sec.gov refuses automated requests whose User-Agent does not give a contact email address, and the project's scripts send none. `check_quotes.py` therefore does not fetch sec.gov and reports these rows as fetch failed. The quotes were checked in excerpts returned by a summarising web fetch, which is not a character-for-character comparison. Apple was compared character for character against a saved copy of the filing.

The docs workflow reruns it on every pull request and compares the output byte for byte.

| C16 | Care.com's year and quarter rules give different Q4 ends in 2020, 2021 and 2025–2027 (window 2019–2028) | [2020, 2021, 2025, 2026, 2027]; 2025: 27 Dec 2025 against 3 Jan 2026. Compares two rules as written; Care.com has used a calendar year since fiscal 2019. | Script check | Verified (under the inclusive reading) | 1 Nov 2026 |
| C17 | The C16 result depends on the reading and the window | Strict reading adds 2022; the inclusive reading over 2010–2035 adds 2010, 2014, 2015, 2031 and 2032 | Script check (informational) | Verified (see D11 on the [PDR](https://github.com/Karthik-beta/fiscalclock/wiki/PDR#open-questions)) | 1 Nov 2026 |
| C18 | `date(9999, 12, 31) + timedelta(days=1)` raises `OverflowError` in Python | `OverflowError: date value out of range` | Script check | Verified | 1 Nov 2026 |
| C19 | The NRF rule gives exactly the 53-week years NRF publishes for 2006–2023; NRF lists none after fiscal 2023, so 2028 (C03) is the rule's prediction only | Rule gives [2006, 2012, 2017, 2023]; NRF publishes [2006, 2012, 2017, 2023] | Script check | Verified | 1 Nov 2026 |

## Unverified claims

These four claims from the research documents have no authoritative source as of 1 Nov 2026. The wiki marks them unverified wherever they appear and does not rely on them for any requirement.

| Claim | Where it appears | What was found | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Thai government fiscal years are numbered in the Buddhist Era (CE + 543) | Proposal, naming axis | Only [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thai_solar_calendar) gives the 543-year difference ("543 years ahead of the Gregorian calendar"); no source says fiscal years are numbered this way | Unverified |
| "Many Japanese companies" name April 2025 to March 2026 "FY2025" | Proposal, naming axis | No source found | Unverified |
| "FY 2025-26" naming is common in the UK and Australia | Proposal, naming axis | No source found | Unverified |
| Nepal's fiscal year starts on 16, 17 or 18 July | Proposal and gap analysis | Only a user comment on the [Akaunting forum](https://akaunting.com/forum/discussion/general/the-fiscal-date-change-every-year), which says "sometime July 16, or July 17 or July 18" | Unverified |

The Indian FY/AY claim was on this list in the plan (contradiction D10). It now has an official source, which corrects it (see [India, ERP and transition years](#india-erp-and-transition-years)).
